target.title: fix(agents): preserve fresh tool results during aggregate recovery
target.body:
Fixes #99481
Related: #96857, #98955

## What Problem This Solves

`#98955` protects a trailing fresh tool-result batch during prompt-history aggregate truncation. `#99481` shows the empty tool-result symptom can still happen on `2026.7.1-beta.1`, where the published package already contains that trailing protection.

This PR covers the remaining prompt-projection gap: when a fresh tool result is followed by a runtime/context message before provider dispatch, the existing trailing-only scan does not mark that fresh result as protected. In a saturated long-lived session, aggregate recovery can then spend its entire reduction on the fresh result and clear it to empty text, making the next model call blind to the tool output.

## Implementation

- Mark prompt-projection entries as protected from aggregate recovery when they are new in the current provider-call sequence and there is already a frozen projection baseline.
- Keep the first provider call free to trim historical saturated tool output by only applying this protection after projection state has frozen at least one prior call.
- Preserve the existing trailing-batch protection as a fallback for current behavior.
- Add regression coverage where saturated history is followed by a fresh `exec`-style tool result and then a runtime context message; the fresh output remains visible, the aggregate budget stays capped, and older historical tool results are the entries reduced first.

## Evidence

- Source check: installed `2026.7.1-beta.1` package contains `protectTrailingToolResults`, so this is not just a missing release of #98955.
- Local pre-check on PR head `b542fdc042e4c9f4437522ac016eeeddb4a358f5`: `git diff --check -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` passed.
- After-fix behavior proof on PR head `b542fdc042e4c9f4437522ac016eeeddb4a358f5`: a direct helper run with saturated historical tool results, a fresh `fresh_exec` tool result, and a following runtime-context-like user message produced:
  - `freshVisibleText: "ABC"`
  - `freshPreservedAfterRuntimeContext: true`
  - `aggregateToolResultChars: 32000`
  - `aggregateBudgetChars: 32000`
  - `aggregateCapHeld: true`
  - `historicalToolResultsReduced: true`
- GitHub Actions on PR head `b542fdc042e4c9f4437522ac016eeeddb4a358f5`: latest check table finished `66 pass / 28 skip / 0 fail / 0 pending`.
- GitHub Actions regression-test evidence on the previous equivalent head `22e36a030f926bb13645b4707c52df72fe7785f4`: `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1` ran `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts` with 43 tests passing. The current head only rebases on latest `main`, adds explanatory comments, and strengthens the regression assertion to require historical tool results to be reduced while the fresh result remains visible.

## Risk

Low to moderate. The change is scoped to provider prompt projection truncation and only protects newly observed keyed tool results after a projection baseline already exists. Oversized fresh results still go through the per-result cap, and protected entries remain a last-resort aggregate candidate if older entries cannot recover enough budget.

The intended tradeoff is that saturated sessions now reduce older projected tool-result history before reducing the current fresh tool output. That favors model-visible current tool output over older history when both cannot fit in the aggregate budget.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented and reviewed with Codex.
